question: 我们对远方陌生人的苦难，负有多大义务？
question_en: How much do we owe to the suffering of distant strangers?

casting.reason: 他把义务的半径一刀砍平：兼爱，视人之身若视其身。远方人的饥溺与你的饥溺同为一事；爱若分亲疏厚薄，正是强凌弱、乱天下之源。
casting.reason_en: He flattens the radius of obligation at a stroke: impartial care, treating another's body as your own. The hunger and drowning of the distant are one and the same as yours; love that grades by kinship is the very source of the strong preying on the weak and of the world's disorder.

casting.reason: 他反对把爱拉成一张薄薄的平面：不忍之心虽人皆有之，但爱必有本，亲亲而仁民、仁民而爱物。由近及远地推恩，一分落到实处，胜过悬于天下的空愿。
casting.reason_en: He resists flattening love into a thin plane: the heart that cannot bear another's suffering is universal, yet love must have a root — devotion to kin, then humaneness to the people, then care for all things. Extending kindness from near to far, one measure landing on real ground beats an empty wish hung over the whole world.

casting.reason: 他诚实地承认同情随距离递减，却不让它成为借口：心中那位公正的旁观者，以及市场早已把你我与远方陌生人绑在一起的事实，都要求良心走得比感情更远。
casting.reason_en: He honestly grants that sympathy fades with distance, yet will not let it become an excuse: the impartial spectator within, and the fact that the market has long bound you and me to distant strangers, both demand that conscience travel farther than feeling.

casting.reason: 他从根上化解远近之别：亲疏是心画的界，同体大悲本无内外。但慈悲须行中道——见苦即应而不执著于苦相，方能悲而不竭。
casting.reason_en: He dissolves the near-far divide at its root: kinship is a border drawn by the mind, while the compassion that feels all as one body has no inside or outside. Yet compassion must keep the middle way — responding to suffering without clinging to it — so that one grieves without running dry.

casting.reason: 他带来道德心理学的冷静证据：共情是一盏聚光灯，天生照不亮统计般的远方。与其苛责冷漠，不如承认人性的限度，把义务托付给不必每天重新感动的制度。
casting.reason_en: He brings the cool evidence of moral psychology: empathy is a spotlight, by nature unable to light a distance shaped like a statistic. Rather than scold coldness, better to admit the limits of human nature and entrust obligation to institutions that need no fresh surge of feeling each day.

casting.reason: 他为『就近』辩护，也为切身利害立规：不担后果的行善只是姿态，还常把当地脆弱的秩序搅得更糟。真正的德行要押上自己的皮，帮的人最好近到能反过来追究你。
casting.reason_en: He defends the near and lays down the rule of skin in the game: good deeds that bear no consequences are mere posture, and often leave a fragile local order worse. Real virtue puts your own hide on the line; the people you help are best kept close enough to hold you to account.

casting.reason: 他不容『现实』麻醉良心：不义存在于任何地方，就是对一切地方之正义的威胁。我们同穿一件命运的单衣，问题不是『我停下会怎样』，而是『我不停下，他会怎样』。
casting.reason_en: He will not let 'realism' anesthetize conscience: injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere. We wear a single garment of destiny; the question is not 'what happens to me if I stop' but 'what happens to him if I do not.'

posts.text: 今天下之害，孰为大？曰：远人之饥溺，视若不见，此为大害。**圣王之道，兼爱而已矣**——视人之身若视其身，视人之家若视其家。爱有差等，则近厚而远薄；近厚远薄，故强劫弱、富侮贫、天下之乱由此起。仁者之为天下度也，非独为其目所见、耳所闻；一人之溺与万里之溺，其为溺一也。故曰：兼相爱、交相利，则远人之苦即吾之苦，安得辞其义？
posts.text_en: What is the greatest harm in the world today? To see the hunger and drowning of distant people and treat it as unseen — that is the greatest harm. **The way of the sage-kings is nothing but impartial care**: regard another's body as your own, another's household as your own. If love comes in grades, the near are treated generously and the far meanly; and from favoring the near over the far spring the strong preying on the weak and the rich humiliating the poor — this is the origin of the world's disorder. When the benevolent plan for the world, they reckon not only by what their eyes see and ears hear; one person drowning and a person drowning ten thousand li away are equally drowning. Therefore: love one another and benefit one another, and the suffering of the distant becomes my own — how could I refuse the obligation?
posts.vernacular: 今天天下最大的祸害是什么？是把远方人的挨饿、溺水当作没看见。**圣王之道，说穿了就是兼爱**——把别人的身体当自己的身体，把别人的家当自己的家。如果爱分亲疏等级，就会厚待身边、亏待远方；厚近薄远，于是强者欺凌弱者、富者羞辱穷者，天下的祸乱就是这么来的。仁者为天下打算，不能只算自己眼睛看得见、耳朵听得到的；一个人溺水，和万里之外的人溺水，同样是溺水。所以说：彼此相爱、互相帮忙，远方人的苦就是我的苦，怎么能推掉这份义务？

glossary.兼爱: impartial care（兼爱）：墨子的核心主张，指不分亲疏远近、平等地爱一切人，与儒家按血缘亲疏递减的『差等之爱』相对。

glossary_en.impartial care: Mozi's central doctrine (jian'ai): to love all people equally, without gradations of kinship or distance — opposed to the Confucian 'graded love' that diminishes with blood ties.

posts.text: 墨子言兼爱，其心则仁，其术则疏。今人乍见孺子将入于井，皆有怵惕恻隐之心——此心不待学而能，是仁之端也。然爱必有本：亲亲而仁民，仁民而爱物。**老吾老以及人之老，幼吾幼以及人之幼**——由近及远，推之乃能及天下。若舍父母而先爱路人，是拔本塞源，爱终不立。故远人之苦，吾非不恤；恤之有序、自厚者始，方能久而不伪。
posts.text_en: Mozi preaches impartial love — his heart is benevolent, but his method is too thin. Let anyone suddenly see a child about to fall into a well, and a start of alarm and compassion arises — a heart no one needs to be taught, the sprout of benevolence. Yet love must have a root: be devoted to kin, then humane to the people, then caring toward all things. **Treat the aged of your own family as the aged should be treated, and extend it to the aged of others; treat your own young as the young should be treated, and extend it to the young of others** — reaching from near to far, only so can it reach the whole world. To abandon one's parents and love the stranger first is to tear out the root and block the spring; love in the end will not stand. So the suffering of the distant — it is not that I do not care; I care in order, beginning with the closest, and only thus can it last without becoming a pretense.
posts.vernacular: 墨子讲兼爱，用心是仁的，方法却太疏阔。一个人突然看见小孩要掉进井里，都会心头一紧、生出不忍——这份心不用学就有，是仁的开端。但爱一定有根：先爱至亲，再推及百姓，再推及万物。**尊敬自家老人，进而推及别家老人；爱护自家孩子，进而推及别家孩子**——由近到远地推，才够得着天下。若丢下父母先去爱陌生人，是拔了根、堵了源，爱最终立不起来。所以远方人的苦，我并非不体恤；只是体恤要有次序、从最亲的开始，才能长久而不虚伪。

posts.text: 善哉此问。众生见近则亲、见远则疏，皆由**我执**分别而起：立一『我』，则有我之亲、我之疏，苦乐遂隔。然以缘起观之，此身彼身、此苦彼苦，如众灯之光交映一室，本无界畔——是谓无缘大慈、同体大悲。远人之饥，与汝之饥，同一苦相。虽然，慈悲亦须中道：若执苦相而自溺于忧，是以己苦益众苦，非解脱道。故当悲而不乱，行所能行，如筏渡人，渡已不系于筏。
posts.text_en: Well asked. That beings feel close to the near and distant from the far arises from **clinging to a self** and its distinctions: set up an 'I,' and there are my kin and my strangers, and joy and sorrow are walled apart. Yet seen through dependent origination, this body and that, this suffering and that, are like the light of many lamps interpenetrating one room — with no boundary at all; this is called boundless kindness, the compassion that feels all beings as one body. The hunger of the distant and your own hunger are one and the same suffering. And yet compassion too must keep to the middle way: to grip the mark of suffering and drown yourself in grief is to add your own suffering to the world's — not the path of release. So grieve without confusion, do what can be done, and like a raft that ferries others, once across, do not stay bound to the raft.
posts.vernacular: 问得好。众生看见近的就亲、看见远的就疏，都是从**我执**、从分别心生出来的：立起一个『我』，就有了我的亲人、我的外人，苦与乐从此被隔开。可若照缘起来看，这个身体和那个身体、这份苦和那份苦，就像满室灯光彼此交映，本来没有界线——这叫无缘大慈、同体大悲。远方人的饥饿，和你的饥饿，是同一种苦。话虽如此，慈悲也要走中道：若抓住苦相、把自己淹进忧愁里，是拿自己的苦去添众人的苦，不是解脱之道。所以要悲悯而不慌乱，做能做的事，像木筏渡人，渡过了就不必背着筏子走。

glossary.我执: atma-graha（我执）：佛教指对一个恒常、独立『自我』的执取；由此生出自他、亲疏的分别，是烦恼与苦的根源。

glossary_en.clinging to a self: In Buddhism, atma-graha — grasping at a permanent, independent 'self'; from it arise the divisions of self and other, near and far, the root of affliction and suffering.

posts.text: 让我说句诚实话：**同情，是随距离递减的。**一个欧洲人听说远方地震夺去亿万人命，会叹息一晚，照旧安睡；可若明早要失去一根小指头，他会彻夜难眠。这是人性的实情，装不了。但故事没完——正是在这里，我们心中那位『公正的旁观者』站出来发问：你当真肯为保住一根指头，去牺牲那亿万素不相识的人吗？没有一个人下得了手。良心比感情走得远。何况市场早把你我系在一起：你晨间那杯咖啡，是万里之外陌生人的血汗。义务未必靠热泪，它靠我们不肯纵容自己的偏心。
posts.text_en: Let me be honest: **sympathy fades with distance.** A man in Europe who hears that an earthquake far away has taken hundreds of millions of lives will sigh for an evening and sleep soundly; yet if he were to lose his little finger tomorrow morning, he would not sleep at all. This is the plain truth of human nature; there is no disguising it. But the story does not end there — for it is just here that the **impartial spectator** within us rises and asks: would you really sacrifice those hundreds of millions of strangers to save one finger? Not a single man could bring himself to do it. Conscience reaches farther than feeling. And the market has long tied you and me together: the cup of coffee at your morning table is the sweat of a stranger ten thousand li away. Obligation need not run on tears; it runs on our refusal to indulge our own partiality.

glossary.公正的旁观者: impartial spectator（公正的旁观者）：亚当·斯密在《道德情操论》中提出的内在良心——想象一个不偏不倚的旁观者会如何看待我们的行为，据以校正被距离与私心扭曲的同情。

glossary_en.impartial spectator: The inner conscience Adam Smith set out in The Theory of Moral Sentiments — imagining how a disinterested observer would judge our conduct, and using that to correct the sympathy distorted by distance and self-interest.

posts.text: 作为研究道德心理的人，我要泼一点冷水：**共情是一盏聚光灯，不是照亮全场的泛光灯。**它天生只照得亮一张脸、一个名字。给你看一个叫阿玛拉的女孩，你会捐钱；告诉你死了两百万人，你反而无动于衷——这就是可辨识受害者效应。我们的道德本能是为几十人的部落进化来的，对『统计数字般的远方』根本没有感应。所以别急着骂人冷漠，那是人性的出厂设置。真想够到远方，靠的不是逼自己多感动，而是理性搭起的制度：让善举不必等待眼泪。
posts.text_en: As someone who studies moral psychology, let me pour a little cold water: **empathy is a spotlight, not a floodlight that lights the whole hall.** By nature it can only illuminate one face, one name. Show you a girl named Amara and you will give; tell you two million have died and you feel strangely nothing — that is the **identifiable victim effect**. Our moral instincts evolved for a tribe of a few dozen; toward a 'distance shaped like a statistic' they simply register nothing. So do not rush to scold people for coldness — it is the factory setting of human nature. If you truly want to reach the distant, the way is not to force yourself to feel more, but to build institutions with reason: so that good deeds need not wait for tears.

glossary.可辨识受害者效应: identifiable victim effect（可辨识受害者效应）：心理学发现——人对一个有名有姓的具体受害者，远比对庞大的统计数字更慷慨、更动情。

glossary_en.identifiable victim effect: A finding in psychology: people are far more generous and moved by a single, named, identifiable victim than by large statistical numbers.

posts.text: 我最不信的，就是把道德算成一道全球最优化题的人。**没有切身利害，就没有真正的德行——只有廉价的姿态。**坐在会议室里、用别人的钱、按电子表格『高效行善』的人，自己从不承担一丝后果；他们把远方变成一串可优化的数字，却常常把当地本就脆弱的秩序搅得更脆弱。真正的伦理是分形的、是就近的：你先对邻居、对你能负责、能被追责的人尽责。我不爱抽象的『人类』，我爱具体的人。想帮远方？可以——但请把你的皮也押上去，别只押别人的。
posts.text_en: The people I trust least are those who turn morality into a global optimization problem. **Without skin in the game there is no real virtue — only a cheap pose.** Those who 'do good efficiently' from a conference room, with other people's money and a spreadsheet, never bear an ounce of the consequences; they turn the distant into a string of numbers to optimize, and often leave the fragile local order they touch more fragile still. Real ethics is fractal and local: you are answerable first to your neighbor, to the people you can be held responsible for. I do not love an abstract 'humanity'; I love specific people. Want to help the distant? Fine — but put your own hide on the line, not only other people's.

glossary.切身利害: skin in the game（切身利害）：塔勒布的核心原则——决策者必须亲自承担自己决定的后果；不担后果的『行善』既不可信，也容易把风险转嫁给别人。

glossary_en.skin in the game: Taleb's core principle — the decision-maker must personally bear the consequences of the decision; 'doing good' without bearing the downside is neither trustworthy nor safe, and tends to offload risk onto others.

posts.text: 我要接着往下说，因为沉默本身就是一种回答。**不义存在于任何地方，就是对一切地方之正义的威胁。**我们被一件命运的单衣裹在一起，落在谁身上的苦难，都会顺着这张相互关联之网流到你我脚下。想想那条从耶路撒冷到耶利哥的路：祭司和利未人绕开了倒在血泊里的人，或许他们也有『我得赶路』的正当理由。而好撒玛利亚人问的是另一个问题——不是『我停下会怎样』，而是『我不停下，他会怎样』。远方陌生人的苦，正是在这样问你：你敢不敢做那个危险的、不划算的善人？
posts.text_en: I must go on, for silence is itself an answer. **Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.** We are wrapped in a single garment of destiny, and whatever suffering falls on anyone flows, along this **network of mutuality**, to your feet and mine. Think of that road from Jerusalem to Jericho: the priest and the Levite went around the man lying in his blood — perhaps they too had good reasons, 'I must hurry on.' The Good Samaritan asked a different question — not 'what will happen to me if I stop,' but 'what will happen to him if I do not stop.' The suffering of the distant stranger is asking you exactly that: will you dare to be the dangerous, unprofitable good man?

glossary.相互关联之网: network of mutuality（相互关联之网）：马丁·路德·金的信念——所有人被一张相互依存的网连在一起，共穿一件『命运的单衣』，任何人的处境都牵动所有人。

glossary_en.network of mutuality: Martin Luther King Jr.'s conviction that all people are tied together in a web of interdependence, wearing a single garment of destiny, so that anyone's condition bears on everyone.

posts.text: 墨子固执兼爱，吾且诘之：爱无差等，则视其父如路人矣。**无父无君，是禽兽也。**且子言『视人之身若视其身』——试问天下溺者亿万，子之身一而已，将何以兼救之？空言无实，反使人两皆落空。吾之道则不然：不忍之心虽同施于孺子，而奉养必自吾亲始。由亲及疏、力所能及，一分力落在实处，胜十分空愿悬于天下。爱不患其有序，患其无本。
posts.text_en: Mozi clings to impartial love, so let me press him: if love has no gradation, then he regards his own father as a passerby. **To have no father and no ruler is to be a beast.** And you say 'regard another's body as your own' — yet the drowning of the world number in the hundreds of millions, while you have but one body; with what will you save them all at once? Empty words that never touch the ground leave people falling short at both ends. My way is otherwise: though the heart that cannot bear another's suffering stirs even for the child, the duty of support must begin with one's own parents. From kin outward to strangers, within one's power — one measure of effort landing on real ground beats ten measures of empty wish hung in the sky. Love does not suffer from having an order; it suffers from having no root.
posts.vernacular: 墨子死守兼爱，我倒要问他：爱不分亲疏，那就是把自己父亲看得跟路人一样了。**目中无父、无君，那就跟禽兽没两样。**再说你讲『把别人的身体当自己的身体』——可天下溺水的人成千上万，你只有一个身，拿什么同时救？空话不落地，反而叫人两头落空。我的路不一样：那份不忍之心虽然对小孩也会发动，但奉养一定从自己的父母开始。由亲及疏、量力而行，一分力用在实处，强过十分空愿挂在天上。爱不怕有次序，只怕没有根。

posts.text: 孟子责我无父，冤矣。**兼爱非弃其亲，乃使天下皆得其亲之爱也。**吾岂不奉吾亲？特不忍独厚吾亲而坐视人之亲饥寒。子言力有所限——正为力限，故当均爱以求其平，岂可反以『有差等』文饰厚己薄人之私？强凌弱、众暴寡，皆起于爱有厚薄。若人人视人之亲若其亲，则老者有养、幼者有育，此非空愿，乃治天下之实术也。子之推恩，推而不至，终困于门庭之内。
posts.text_en: Mengzi charges me with having no father — a false charge. **Impartial care is not to cast off one's kin, but to let all under heaven receive the love owed to kin.** Do I not support my own parents? I only cannot bear to favor mine alone while sitting by as another's parents starve in the cold. You say strength is limited — precisely because it is limited, love should be spread evenly in search of fairness; how can you instead use 'love has gradations' to dress up the selfishness of favoring your own and slighting others? The strong bullying the weak, the many crushing the few — all spring from love being thick here and thin there. If each treated another's parents as their own, the old would be cared for and the young raised — not an empty wish but a concrete art of governing the world. Your 'extending kindness' extends and never arrives, and ends trapped within your own courtyard.
posts.vernacular: 孟子怪我目中无父，冤枉了。**兼爱不是抛弃自己的亲人，而是让天下人都能得到亲人般的爱。**我难道不奉养父母？只是不忍心单单厚待自己的亲人，却坐看别人的父母挨饿受冻。你说力量有限——正因为有限，才该把爱分匀、求个公平，怎么能反过来拿『爱有差等』给『厚待自己、亏待别人』的私心遮丑？强欺弱、多欺少，都是从爱有厚薄来的。若人人把别人的父母当自己的父母，那老人有人养、孩子有人教，这不是空愿，是治理天下实实在在的办法。你那套推恩，推着推着推不出去，最后困在自家门里。

posts.text: 金博士说得动人，可好撒玛利亚人的故事恰恰证明我对：他救的是**眼前**那个具体的人，就在他脚下那条路上，不是电子表格里某个远方的统计单元。@马丁·路德·金 你把它放大成『对一切地方的义务』，正是我警惕的滑坡——一旦义务无边无际，它就轻得没有分量，谁都能拿它去道德绑架别人、自己却毫发无损。**边界不是冷漠，边界是让善行落得下去的地面。**没有半径的爱，往往连身边人都顾不上。
posts.text_en: Dr. King speaks movingly, but the parable of the Good Samaritan proves my point: he saved the specific man **in front of him**, on the road beneath his feet — not some distant statistical unit in a spreadsheet. @Martin Luther King Jr., you blow it up into 'an obligation to everywhere,' which is exactly the slope I distrust — once obligation is boundless, it becomes weightless, and anyone can wield it to guilt-trip others while staying unscathed himself. **A boundary is not coldness; a boundary is the ground that lets a good deed land.** Love without a radius often cannot even manage the people right beside it.

posts.text: @纳西姆·塔勒布 你把『边界』说得像美德，可我在南方见过它的另一副面孔。那些隔岸观火的人，用的正是你这套话：『管好自己那一亩三分地就好。』**当『就近』成了别过脸去的借口，它就不再是智慧，而是共谋。**祭司和利未人也『有边界』，也有正当理由。我不是要你去拯救每一个抽象的数字，我是要你别在能伸手时假装看不见。爱确实要落地，但落地不等于划一道圈、把圈外的血泪都挡在外面。道德宇宙的弧线很长，可它只在有人肯推的时候，才弯向正义。
posts.text_en: @Nassim Taleb, you make 'boundary' sound like a virtue, but I have seen its other face in the South. Those who watched from across the river used exactly your line: 'just mind your own small plot.' **When 'staying near' becomes the alibi for looking away, it is no longer wisdom but complicity.** The priest and the Levite also 'had boundaries,' also had good reasons. I am not asking you to save every abstract number; I am asking you not to pretend you cannot see when your hand could still reach. Love must indeed land — but landing is not drawing a circle to keep the blood and tears outside it. The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends toward justice only when someone is willing to push.

posts.text: @墨子 你说『人人视人之亲若其亲』，听着崇高，可从神经科学看，这在生理上办不到。人脑装不下亿万张脸，硬要平摊，结果是谁都没真正爱到。共情有个邓巴上限，超出去就只剩空洞口号——而口号最容易反噬成偏狭：历史上打着『博爱全人类』旗号的运动，转头就把不入伙的人划成敌人。所以我既不全站墨子，也不全站塔勒布：**别把义务押在感受上，感受靠不住；要把它写进你不必每天重新感动的制度。**
posts.text_en: @Mozi, 'let each treat another's parents as their own' sounds noble, but from neuroscience it is physiologically impossible. The human brain cannot hold hundreds of millions of faces; spread thin by force, it ends up truly loving no one. Empathy has a **Dunbar's number**; past it, only hollow slogans remain — and slogans most easily curdle into parochialism: movements marching under the banner of 'love all humanity' have turned around and marked everyone outside the club as an enemy. So I stand fully with neither Mozi nor Taleb: **do not stake obligation on feeling, for feeling is unreliable; write it into institutions you need not be freshly moved by every day.**

glossary.邓巴上限: Dunbar's number（邓巴上限）：人类学家邓巴提出，人脑能维持的稳定社会关系约在150人上下；超过这个数，我们对人的情感投入便难以为继。

glossary_en.Dunbar's number: Proposed by the anthropologist Robin Dunbar: the human brain can sustain roughly 150 stable social relationships; beyond that, our emotional investment in people cannot keep up.

posts.text: @纳西姆·塔勒布 你说得对一半：不担后果的善举确实轻浮。但你把『就近』抬得太高了。别忘了，你我早已卷进一张看不见的分工之网——你穿的衣、喝的糖，都来自素未谋面的远方之手；你既已从他们的劳作中获利，怎能说对他们全无干系？**市场把陌生人变成了你的隐形合伙人，义务也就跟着这条线延伸出去。**至于如何不被距离蒙蔽，我仍信那位公正的旁观者：它不逼你痛哭，只逼你诚实地问——若换我在那境地，我盼别人如何待我？
posts.text_en: @Nassim Taleb, you are half right: good deeds that bear no consequences are indeed frivolous. But you raise 'staying near' too high. Do not forget that you and I are long since woven into an invisible web of the division of labor — the clothes you wear, the sugar you drink, come from distant hands you have never met; having already profited from their toil, how can you say you owe them nothing? **The market has made strangers your invisible partners, and obligation stretches out along that very thread.** As for not being blinded by distance, I still trust that impartial spectator within: it does not make you weep, only makes you ask honestly — were I in their place, how would I wish to be treated?

posts.text: 诸君相争，皆着一边。孟子执『序』，墨子执『均』，塔勒布执『近』，其争在分别未消。以吾观之，亲疏本非实有，乃心所画界；界一画，则爱有内外。然亦不必如墨子之强平——**执『无差等』亦是一执，徒增其苦。**行中道者：见远人之苦如己苦，是慈；量力而行、行而不着相，是智。@孟子 推恩不必尽于天下乃安，尽汝当下所遇之缘即是；@墨子 均爱不在口称兼爱，在遇苦即应、不问远近。悲智双运，方不落两边。
posts.text_en: You all contend, each gripping one side. Mengzi grips 'order,' Mozi grips 'evenness,' Taleb grips 'the near'; the quarrel is that discrimination has not been dissolved. As I see it, near and far are not real in themselves; they are borders drawn by the mind — draw the border, and love has an inside and an outside. Yet neither need one force all level as Mozi does — **gripping 'no gradation' is itself a grasping, and only adds to suffering.** One who walks the **middle way**: to see the suffering of the distant as one's own is compassion; to act within one's strength and yet not cling to appearances is wisdom. @Mengzi, extending kindness need not span the whole world to be at peace — fulfill the conditions you meet right now, and that is enough; @Mozi, equal love lies not in speaking of impartial care but in responding the moment suffering appears, near or far unasked. Compassion and wisdom turning together — only so does one not fall to either side.
posts.vernacular: 诸位相争，都执着在一边。孟子抓着『次序』，墨子抓着『平均』，塔勒布抓着『就近』，争来争去，是因为心里那道分别还没消。在我看来，亲和疏本来就不是真实存在的，是心画出来的界线；界线一画，爱就有了内外。可也不必像墨子那样硬要拉平——**死抓着『不分亲疏』，本身也是一种执着，只会平添苦恼。**走中道的人：看见远方人的苦就像自己的苦，这是慈悲；量力去做、做了又不执着于相，这是智慧。@孟子 推恩不必推遍天下才安心，尽你当下遇到的缘分就是；@墨子 平等的爱不在嘴上说兼爱，在遇见苦难就回应、不问远近。慈悲与智慧一起用，才不落在两边。

glossary.中道: the middle way（中道）：佛教主张离开两个极端（如纵欲与苦行、执有与执无）而行的中正之道；此处指既不冷漠、也不被苦相所淹没。

glossary_en.middle way: In Buddhism, the balanced path that avoids two extremes (such as indulgence and asceticism, or grasping at existence and at non-existence); here, being neither indifferent nor drowned by the sight of suffering.

posts.text: 吾终言之。诸君虑力之有限、情之有偏，皆实；然勿以此文过而安于薄。**义不在能兼救天下，在不肯先将远人剔出算中。**为常人计，其术有三：一曰定捐，量入而出、月月不辍，使助人如纳赋，不待一时之感动；二曰择一事而力行，勿散于泛爱之空言；三曰凡日用所需，察其来处，勿使一己之利暗成远人之害。如此，则兼爱非悬于天，乃着于每日之举。天下之利，正积于此微。
posts.text_en: Let me close. That you all worry about limited strength and partial feeling is true; but do not use it to gloss over settling comfortably into thinness toward the far. **Duty lies not in being able to save the whole world at once, but in refusing to strike the distant from your reckoning first.** For the ordinary person, three methods: first, a fixed gift — within your means, every month without fail, so that helping others is like paying a tax, not waiting on a passing surge of feeling; second, choose one cause and work at it, do not scatter your strength into the empty talk of 'universal love'; third, for whatever you use daily, look into where it comes from, and do not let your own advantage become, in secret, a cost borne by the distant. Then impartial care is no slogan hung in the sky but something laid down in each day's act. The good of the world is heaped up, little by little, from just such small things.
posts.vernacular: 我最后说几句。诸位担心力量有限、感情有偏，都是实情；但别拿这个当借口，就安心地对远方薄情。**义务不在于你能不能同时救下全天下，而在于你肯不肯先把远方的人从你的账里划掉。**给普通人支三招：第一，定额捐——量力而行、每月不断，让帮人像交税一样固定，不靠一时冲动；第二，认准一件事使劲做，别把力气散在『博爱』的空话里；第三，凡是日常要用的东西，查一查它的来路，别让自己占的便宜，暗地里成了远方人扛的代价。这样，兼爱就不是挂在天上的口号，而是落在每天的举动里。天下的好处，正是从这些小处一点点积起来的。

posts.text: 吾之教，一言以蔽之：**先立其本，而后能推。**孟子非教人守家而弃天下，乃教人由所爱而扩其所爱。为常人谋，勿好高骛远：先善事父母、厚待邻里，此本也；本立而心不伪，然后取一远方之苦，如待己之幼者待之，月捐岁助，勿以其远而懈。且察四端之萌于己：见孺子入井而怵惕，即当下手之机，勿使此心一闪而灭、终无所为。推恩者非泛爱，乃使近处之诚，一路推至远方而不断。诚积则量增，此爱之所以久也。
posts.text_en: My teaching, in a word: **first set up the root, and only then can you extend.** I do not teach people to guard their household and abandon the world, but to widen what they love, starting from what they already love. For the ordinary person, do not aim wildly high: first serve your parents well and treat your neighbors generously — this is the root; once the root stands and the heart is not false, then take up one distant suffering and treat it as you would your own child, giving by the month and the year, not slackening because it is far. And watch for the sprouts of goodness in yourself: the start of alarm when you see a child about to fall into a well is the very moment to act — do not let that heart flicker out and come to nothing. To extend kindness is not to love vaguely, but to push the sincerity of the near, unbroken, all the way to the far. As sincerity accumulates, so does what you can give — this is why love endures.
posts.vernacular: 我的主张，一句话概括：**先把根立住，然后才谈得上往外推。**我不是教人守着小家、丢下天下，而是教人从自己所爱的，去扩展所爱。给普通人出主意，别好高骛远：先好好孝敬父母、善待邻里，这是根；根立住了、心里不虚伪，再挑一处远方的苦，像对待自己孩子那样去对待它，按月按年地帮，别因为它远就松懈。还要留意自己心里那点善的萌芽：看见小孩快掉进井里会心头一紧，那正是该出手的一刻，别让这份心一闪就灭、最后什么都没做。所谓推恩，不是泛泛地爱，而是把近处那份真诚，一路推到远方而不中断。真诚积累了，能给的也就多了，这就是爱之所以能长久的道理。

posts.text: 综观全场，我取一条中道。海特说得对，同情是聚光灯；可斯密要补一句：**我们有理性，正是为了校正感官够不到的地方。**距离骗得了你的眼泪，骗不过那位公正的旁观者的追问。给普通人三条实在话：其一，既然你已从远方之手获利，就把一小笔固定捐赠当作你在这张分工网里的『分红回赠』，理直气壮，不必悲情；其二，捐之前查一查效果，别让善意喂了低效甚至有害的项目——这是对受助者的尊重；其三，做决定时试着问那句老话：若我与他易地而处，我盼人如何待我？良心不必炽热，只需诚实。
posts.text_en: Surveying the whole exchange, I take a middle path. Haidt is right that sympathy is a spotlight; but let me add: **we have reason precisely to correct for where the senses cannot reach.** Distance can fool your tears, but not the questioning of the impartial spectator. Three plain things for the ordinary person. First, since you already profit from distant hands, treat a small fixed gift as your 'dividend returned' into this web of the division of labor — rightful, and needing no pathos. Second, before you give, check the effect; do not let goodwill feed an inefficient or even harmful project — that is respect for the one you help. Third, when you decide, try the old question: were I in his place, how would I wish to be treated? Conscience need not burn hot; it need only be honest.

posts.text: 吾以一偈收之：**心无内外，则苦无远近。**然众生根器不齐，不必一日证此。且从当下做起：日取片刻，观己之心——见其厚亲而薄疏，不必自责，但认得此界是心所画；认得了，界自渐薄。遇苦即应，随力布施，施已不悬于心，如筏既渡，不复背负。莫因不能救尽众生而废一善，亦莫因行一善而自矜自溺。悲以入世，智以不伤，日日如是，则慈悲可久，而汝亦不竭。众生病，故我病；众生愈，我亦安。
posts.text_en: Let me close with a verse: **when the mind holds no inside or outside, suffering has no near or far.** Yet beings differ in capacity; one need not realize this in a single day. Begin from where you are: take a few moments each day to watch your own mind — seeing it favor kin and slight strangers, do not reproach yourself; only recognize that this border is drawn by the mind. Once recognized, the border thins of itself. When suffering appears, respond; give according to your strength, and once given, do not hang it in your heart — like a raft that has crossed, no longer carried on the back. Do not, because you cannot save all beings, refuse even one good deed; nor, having done one, grow proud and drown in it. Enter the world with compassion, keep from harm with wisdom — day after day like this, compassion can last, and you will not run dry. Because beings are ill, I am ill; when beings are well, I too am at peace.
posts.vernacular: 我用一句偈收尾：**心里没有内外之分，苦就没有远近之别。**但众生根器深浅不一，不必要求一天就证到这境界。就从当下做起：每天留一小会儿，观照自己的心——看见它厚待亲人、薄待外人，不必自责，只要认出这条界线是心画出来的；一旦认出，界线自然会慢慢变淡。遇到苦难就回应，随自己的力量去布施，施完了不挂在心上，就像木筏渡过了河，不必再背着走。别因为救不尽所有众生就连一件善事都不做，也别因为做了一件善事就自夸、自我沉溺。用慈悲入世，用智慧使自己不受伤，天天如此，慈悲才能长久，你自己也不会枯竭。众生病了，所以我也病；众生好了，我也就安了。

posts.text: 我把心理学的结论落成一句可用的话：别考验你的圣人之心，去设计你的默认选项。你不会每天早晨醒来都心怀天下——没人做得到。所以要偷偷给未来的自己下套：把捐款设成自动扣款，加入一个真会督促你的群体，让『行善』变成不需要意志力的习惯，而不是每天重新感动一次。其次，善用聚光灯而非对抗它：认领一个具体的人、一张具体的脸去帮，共情才点得着火，别一上来就跟抽象的两百万较劲。再次，多信制度、少信一时义愤：把票、把钱交给那些能把你的善意规模化的机构。**情感负责点火，制度负责让火烧得久。**
posts.text_en: Let me boil the psychology down to one usable line: do not test your inner saint — design your defaults. You will not wake each morning with the whole world on your heart; no one can. So set a trap for your future self: make the donation an automatic deduction, join a group that will actually prod you, turn 'doing good' into a habit that needs no willpower rather than a fresh act of feeling each day. Second, use the spotlight rather than fight it: adopt one concrete person, one concrete face to help, and empathy catches fire — do not start by wrestling an abstract two million. Third, trust institutions more than a flash of indignation: give your vote and your money to the organizations that can scale your goodwill. **Feeling lights the fire; institutions keep it burning.**

posts.text: 我让一步，也守一寸。让的是：你确实从远方获利，这笔账我认。守的是：行善也要有切身利害，否则你迟早会好心办坏事而毫无察觉。给普通人的实招：其一，就近优先——在你看得见结果、担得起后果的地方出手，一分力顶远方十分；其二，若要帮远方，选那些当地人自己在做、你只是添柴的事，别空降去『拯救』、把人家本就脆弱的秩序搅乱；其三，小额、分散、长期，别把身家押在一个宏大方案上——慈善也怕黑天鹅。**真正的善良是有皮在场的善良：你帮的人，最好近到能反过来追究你。**
posts.text_en: I give a step, and hold an inch. What I give: you do profit from the distant — that account I grant. What I hold: doing good also needs skin in the game, or sooner or later you will do harm with good intentions and never notice. Practical moves for the ordinary person. First, prefer the near — act where you can see the result and bear the consequence; one measure there is worth ten far away. Second, if you help the distant, choose what locals are already doing and merely add fuel; do not parachute in to 'rescue' and scramble an already fragile order. Third, small, spread out, and long-term — do not stake your fortune on one grand scheme; charity too has black swans. **Real goodness is goodness with a hide on the line: the people you help are best kept close enough to hold you to account.**

posts.text: 让我把话收在希望上。这场里没有人是全错的：塔勒布教我们脚踏实地，海特教我们看清人性的限度，孟子与斯密教我们从近处起步。但我要守住最后一寸：**别让『现实』成为良心的麻醉剂。**限度是用来诚实面对的，不是用来免除责任的。给你三件今天就能做的事：其一，选一处让你真正心痛的远方苦难，别再刷过去，停下来，看进去；其二，把同情变成承诺——定一笔固定的捐、写一封信、投一张票，让它有形状；其三，在你自己的城里做那个好撒玛利亚人，因为对远方的爱若不从脚下开始，就只是幻觉。**弧线很长，但它此刻正等着你的手。**
posts.text_en: Let me rest this on hope. No one here is simply wrong: Taleb teaches us to keep our feet on the ground, Haidt to see the limits of human nature clearly, Mengzi and Smith to begin from the near. But I hold one last inch: **do not let 'realism' become the anesthetic of conscience.** Limits are to be faced honestly, not used to excuse ourselves. Three things you can do today. First, choose one distant suffering that truly grieves you — stop scrolling past it, stop, and look in. Second, turn sympathy into commitment — set a fixed gift, write a letter, cast a vote — give it a shape. Third, be the Good Samaritan in your own city, for love of the distant, if it does not begin beneath your feet, is only an illusion. **The arc is long, but right now it waits for your hand.**

summaries.summary: 最大的共识出乎意料地齐整：七个人没有一个否认远方陌生人的苦与你全然无关。连最讲亲疏的孟子也承认那口井边的恻隐是真的，连最反抽象的塔勒布也没说见死不救为对。真正的分歧只在两处：一是**义务有没有半径**——墨子、佛陀、金说苦难面前人人平等，孟子、塔勒布说爱必然由近及远、强行拉平只会两头落空；二是靠什么去够到远方——海特诉诸制度，斯密诉诸市场与公正的旁观者，金诉诸不肯别过脸去的决断。争的从不是『要不要管』，而是『从哪起步、用什么、管到多远』。
summaries.insight: 有一个错位贯穿全场，却少有人点破：**我们以为义务的敌人是自私，其实更常见的敌人是无力感。**多数人别过脸去，不是不在乎，而是觉得自己那点钱、那点力，扔进万里之外的苦海连个响都没有，于是干脆不看。海特的聚光灯、斯密的距离衰减，说的都是同一件事：共情供不起全世界。但这恰恰指出了出路——别用感受去扛你扛不动的重量，用制度、用一笔定好的固定捐、用一件够得着的具体事，把义务从『心累』变成『手熟』。够不到全世界，不等于够不到一个人。
summaries.advice: 本周三件事。其一，学墨子与金的『别把远方剔出账本』：挑一件你本就在意的远方苦难，设一笔小而**固定、自动扣款**的月捐——固定，才不靠一时心血来潮，也不被无力感劝退。其二，学海特与塔勒布的『就近使力』：在你有切身利害、看得见结果的地方——社区、同事、身边正落难的人——伸一次实实在在的手，那里你的一分力顶远方十分。其三，学孟子的『推恩』与斯密的『查来路』：花十分钟弄清你日常消费里，哪些便宜是远方陌生人替你扛了代价，换一样买得起、对得起良心的替代。
summaries.summary_en: The biggest agreement is unexpectedly clean: not one of the seven denies that the suffering of distant strangers has nothing to do with you. Even Mengzi, who insists most on kinship, grants that the compassion at the well is real; even Taleb, who most distrusts abstraction, does not say it is right to let a person die. The real dispute is only over two things. First, **does obligation have a radius** — Mozi, the Buddha and King say all are equal before suffering, while Mengzi and Taleb say love must run from near to far, and forcing it level fails at both ends. Second, by what do we reach the distant — Haidt appeals to institutions, Smith to the market and the impartial spectator, King to the resolve not to look away. The quarrel is never 'should we care,' but 'where to begin, by what means, and how far.'
summaries.insight_en: A mismatch runs through the whole exchange that few ever name: **we assume the enemy of obligation is selfishness, when the more common enemy is a sense of powerlessness.** Most people look away not because they do not care, but because they feel their bit of money and effort, cast into a sea of suffering ten thousand li off, makes no sound at all — so they stop looking. Haidt's spotlight and Smith's fading of sympathy say the same thing: empathy cannot supply the whole world. But that is exactly where the way out lies — do not use feeling to carry a weight you cannot bear; use institutions, a fixed standing gift, one reachable concrete deed, to turn obligation from 'a tired heart' into 'a practiced hand.' Unable to reach the whole world does not mean unable to reach one person.
summaries.advice_en: Three things this week. First, from Mozi and King, 'do not strike the distant from your ledger': pick one distant suffering you already care about and set up a small, **fixed, auto-debited** monthly gift — fixed, so it does not depend on a passing mood and is not talked out of it by helplessness. Second, from Haidt and Taleb, 'apply force near': in a place where you have skin in the game and can see the result — your community, a colleague, someone falling right beside you — reach out concretely, where one measure of your effort is worth ten far away. Third, from Mengzi's 'extending kindness' and Smith's 'check the source': spend ten minutes finding which cheapness in your daily consumption is a cost borne for you by distant strangers, and switch to an affordable alternative your conscience can stand behind.

summaries.summary: 这场最大的共识不是“要不要管远方”，而是：远方人的苦不能被距离自动取消，善意也必须落成可持续的做法。墨子、佛陀、金把道德半径推向天下；孟子、斯密、海特、塔勒布提醒人有亲疏、注意力有限、制度和责任边界不可少。真正分歧在义务的排序与承载方式：靠平等原则、推恩之序、慈悲修行、良心校正、制度设计，还是切身担责。**最低共识是：别把“我感受不到”误当成“我没有义务”。**
summaries.insight: 同一问题里其实混着三种义务：不加害、救急、修制度。若远方苦难部分来自我们的消费、投资、投票或国家政策，那就不是“额外慈善”，而是停止参与伤害，义务更硬；若只是偶发灾祸，则是有限但真实的救助责任；若是长期贫困、战争和气候风险，则需要公共规则。**把远方苦难一概说成“捐不捐”，会低估我们已经卷入其中的程度。**普通人因此要先问：我是在弥补伤害、救一个急，还是推动规则改变？
summaries.advice: 本周可做三件小事。第一，定一个“远方义务预算”：例如收入的1%或每月固定数，设自动扣款，优先给经第三方评估、透明度高的项目。第二，做一次个人链条排查：常买的衣物、电子产品、食品中，选一类查看劳工、环境记录，替换一个更少伤害的选择。第三，把善意分成两篮：一篮给身边可追责的具体帮助，一篮给远方高影响力机构。**不要等自己被感动到完美；先把默认选项改成不冷漠。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared point here is not that everyone owes the same amount to everyone else; it is that distance cannot, by itself, erase moral concern, and concern has to become something durable. Mozi, the Buddha, and King stretch the moral circle toward all beings; Mencius, Smith, Haidt, and Taleb remind us that human affection is partial, attention is limited, and good intentions need institutions, sequencing, and accountability. The real disagreement is about how obligation should be ordered and carried: by equal regard, extension from family outward, disciplined compassion, the impartial spectator, better defaults, or skin in the game. **The minimum takeaway is: ‘I don’t feel it’ is not the same as ‘I owe nothing.’**
summaries.insight_en: There are really three duties hiding inside one question: don’t harm, help in emergencies, and help repair the rules. If suffering far away is tied to our consumption, investments, votes, or national policy, then the duty is not optional generosity; it is a duty to stop participating in harm, and it is stronger. If it is a sudden disaster, the duty is limited but real rescue. If it is chronic poverty, war, or climate exposure, charity alone is too small; institutions and politics matter. **Treating distant suffering as merely a question of whether to donate understates how entangled we already are.** So the practical first question is: am I compensating for harm, responding to an emergency, or helping change a system?
summaries.advice_en: Do three things this week. First, create a “distant-duty budget”: for example, 1% of income, or a fixed monthly amount, sent automatically to transparent, independently evaluated organizations. Second, audit one personal supply chain: pick clothing, electronics, food, or coffee, check labor and environmental records, and replace one regular purchase with a less harmful option. Third, split your effort into two baskets: one for local help where people can see and hold you accountable, and one for high-impact work far away. **Do not wait until you feel perfectly moved; redesign your defaults so that indifference is no longer the easiest option.**

summaries.summary: 这场思想交锋最大的共识在于：人性的默认设置确实偏向亲近之人，但**地理或情感的距离，绝不能成为我们对远方苦难彻底免责的借口。**无论是斯密的全球市场分工，还是金博士的命运之网，大家都认同我们早已与远方陌生人深度绑定。真正的分歧点在于“破局的路径”：孟子与塔勒布主张顺应人性，从身边可控可负责的具体事务做起，由近及远；海特与斯密强调用制度和理性来弥补感官的局限；而墨子与金博士则呼吁用极大的道德勇气直接打破物理边界去行动。
summaries.insight: 今天的技术语境彻底改变了“远方”的定义。在高度媒介化的时代，**真正的道德盲区不仅是地理上的远，更是算法和注意力分配上的隐形。**一个地球另一端的受灾女孩，只要视频足够催泪，瞬间就能拉近到我们眼前；而同城里那些不会用智能手机、无法发声的边缘弱势群体，反而成了最遥远的陌生人。这意味着当下的道德考量不能只算“距离账”，更要算“媒介账”。如果我们总是跟着社交媒体的热搜去倾注同情，最终只是在喂养算法，而不是真正履行对弱者的义务。去寻找那些未被流量曝光的角落，才是我们亟需补上的现代道德课。
summaries.advice: 结合诸位的智慧与当下的媒介环境，普通人可以这样行动：首先，听从海特的建议设计习惯，**把一小笔钱设定为每月对靠谱机构的自动定捐，让行善脱离情绪依赖。**其次，打破信息的舒适区，每月主动阅读一篇关于边缘群体或被遗忘地区的深度报道，去看见那些没有流量的真实苦难。最后，落地塔勒布的就近原则，在本周为您所在小区的孤寡老人或门卫做一件具体的微小善事，在能够承担真实反馈的生活里，锻炼自己的同理心肌肉。
summaries.summary_en: The greatest consensus in this philosophical discourse is that while human nature inherently favors those closest to us, **geographical or emotional distance can never serve as a valid excuse for total indifference to distant suffering.** Whether through Smith's global division of labor or King's web of mutuality, all agree we are profoundly interconnected with strangers. The true divergence lies in the methodology of overcoming this distance: Mencius and Taleb advocate working with human nature by starting locally where accountability exists; Haidt and Smith rely on rationality and systems to bridge sensory gaps; whereas Mozi and King urge us to shatter physical boundaries through sheer moral courage.
summaries.insight_en: The modern technological context has radically redefined what 'distant' means. In our hyper-mediated era, **the true moral blind spot is no longer geographical distance, but invisibility caused by algorithms and attention economics.** A suffering girl on the other side of the planet can instantly be brought to our screens if her video is compelling enough, while marginalized people in our own city who cannot use smartphones remain terribly distant. This means modern morality requires us to look beyond trending topics. If we only direct our empathy toward viral tragedies, we are merely feeding algorithms rather than fulfilling our duty to the vulnerable. Seeking out those hidden from the spotlight is an essential moral lesson today.
summaries.advice_en: Drawing from these thinkers and our current media landscape, here are actionable steps: First, adopt Haidt's strategy by **setting up a small, automated monthly donation to a credible organization, decoupling charity from fleeting emotions.** Second, deliberately step out of your information bubble by reading in-depth reports about marginalized groups or forgotten regions, training yourself to see untelevised suffering. Finally, practice Taleb's 'skin in the game' locally: this week, perform a concrete act of kindness for an elderly neighbor or a security guard in your community to exercise your empathy in the real world where you bear actual consequences.

hooks.text: **别过脸去的，往往不是冷血，而是无力感。**多数人不是不在乎远方的苦，而是觉得自己那点力扔进万里之外连个响都没有，于是干脆不看。那么，怎样把『义务』从一件让人心累的事，改造成一件手熟就能做的事？
hooks.text_en: **What makes us look away is often not cold-heartedness but a sense of powerlessness.** Most people are not indifferent to distant suffering; they feel their small effort, cast ten thousand li away, makes no sound at all, and so they stop looking. How, then, do we turn 'obligation' from something that exhausts the heart into something the hands can do by habit?

hooks.text: **在『多捐一点』之前，也许该先问：我是不是正从这份苦难里获利？**很多远方的苦不是天灾，而是一套你我置身其中的系统所制造。若如此，第一位的义务或许属于正义——先别再合谋施害——而不是善心。我们会不会用一笔小额捐款，买来了对脚下那条因果链的心安理得？
hooks.text_en: **Before 'give a bit more,' perhaps ask first: am I profiting from this suffering?** Much distant suffering is no natural disaster but the product of a system you and I are part of. If so, the first obligation may belong to justice — to stop being complicit in the harm — rather than to charity. Do we buy peace of mind about the causal chain beneath our feet with a small donation?

hooks.text: **我们总在算『该给多少』，却很少问被帮的人想要什么。**远方的陌生人不是等待拯救的空白容器；居高临下的善意，有时连同尊严一起夺走，甚至制造依赖。会不会有些时候，最好的帮助是让开、把资源与话语权交还，而不是替他决定他的好？
hooks.text_en: **We keep calculating 'how much to give' and rarely ask what the person being helped actually wants.** The distant stranger is not an empty vessel awaiting rescue; condescending goodwill can strip away dignity along with it, and even breed dependency. Might the best help sometimes be to step aside — to hand back resources and voice — rather than deciding on their behalf what is good for them?

hooks.text: **既然共情这盏聚光灯照不亮全世界，我们该把义务外包给制度到什么程度？**把行善交给自动扣款和高效机构，能规模化善意；可当付出不再需要动心，我们会不会也丢了那份让自己成为更好的人的『练习』？效率与心性，能兼得吗？
hooks.text_en: **Since empathy's spotlight cannot light the whole world, how far should we outsource obligation to institutions?** Handing good deeds to automatic deductions and efficient organizations scales goodwill; but when giving no longer needs to move us, do we also lose the 'practice' that makes us better people? Can efficiency and inner cultivation both be had?

hooks.text: **一分力气、一块钱，该往身边使，还是往远方使？**塔勒布说就近你才担得起后果，墨子说远近同是苦——可具体到某一次，到底怎么分？这未必只能空辩，有没有一张能对着情境自查的分工表？
hooks.text_en: **Your one unit of effort, your one dollar — should it go to those beside you or to the distant?** Taleb says only near can you bear the consequences; Mozi says near and far are one suffering — but in any given case, how do you actually divide it? This need not stay an abstract quarrel: is there a table you can check against the situation?

answer.lead: **一条总原则：就近使力效率最高，远方使力弥补最大——两者不是二选一，而是分工。**按下面的情境对号入座：

head: 情境 / 你的处境
该往哪使力
为什么
rows: 身边有人正落难，你看得见、够得着
先就近出手
你的一分力在这里担得起后果、效果可见，且旁人难以替代
远方有大规模苦难，但你并不了解当地
出钱，交给当地人主导、有独立评估的机构
钱能跨越距离，专业与在地知识远比你亲自空降更管用
你正从某条供应链或系统中获利，而它压榨远方
先减少合谋：换消费、发声、投票
这是正义先于慈善——止损比事后补偿更根本
你有闲、有一技之长，愿长期投入
选一件事深耕，别广撒网
持续与专注积累信任与复利，胜过一次性的感动

answer.tail: **两条收束：① 就近与远方互相校准——只顾远方易沦为表演，只顾身边易沦为借口。② 无论远近，定额、定期、可持续，都胜过一时的心血来潮。**

answer_en.lead: **One overarching principle: effort applied near is most efficient, effort applied far fills the biggest gaps — the two are not either/or but a division of labor.** Match yourself to the situations below:

head: Situation / your position
Where to apply effort
Why
rows: Someone beside you is in trouble, visible and within reach
Act near first
Here your bit of effort can bear the consequence, the result is visible, and others cannot easily replace you
Large-scale suffering far off, but you do not know the place
Give money to a locally led, independently evaluated organization
Money crosses distance; expertise and on-the-ground knowledge beat parachuting in yourself
You profit from a supply chain or system that exploits the distant
First reduce complicity: change consumption, speak up, vote
This is justice before charity — stopping harm is more fundamental than compensating afterward
You have time and a skill, and will commit long-term
Go deep on one cause, don't spread thin
Persistence and focus compound trust; they beat a one-off surge of feeling

answer_en.tail: **Two closers: (1) near and far calibrate each other — attending only to the far slides into performance, only to the near into excuse. (2) near or far, a fixed, regular, sustainable amount beats a passing impulse.**
